```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea A's category is newly forming. Its listed competitors are recent, some are invite-only or free-only (9pm.ai, Orb), and some have undisclosed commercial pricing (Perch). That leaves more room for a first paying customer than Idea B, where Libsyn, Transistor, Captivate, RSS.com and Castos are mature incumbents.",
    "Idea B faces a hard barrier to switching. Its own brief says moving hosts carries feed-migration risk and fear of losing subscriber history. That makes winning a paying customer within 90 days harder, since that customer must either leave an entrenched host or turn down free-forever tiers.",
    "Idea A has sourced price anchors at $15–75 per month per workspace (display.dev, Volly). Idea B's brief caps realistic ARPU at about $5–20 per month and says free tiers suppress pricing. That ceiling makes Idea B's paid-ads channel ($2–3 Google CPC) harder to justify.",
    "Idea A's acquisition channels are low or zero cost and reach the target audience directly: Product Hunt, Show HN, and Claude/Cursor/MCP directories. A solo operator can use these without an ad budget. Idea B's main channel is paid ads, and its community channel has no sourced cost.",
    "Idea B is described as infrastructure-heavy: storage, bandwidth, CDN, and RSS uptime that must never break, at low margins. That is an ongoing operational burden for one person. Idea A's risks (SSO, sandboxing) can be partly avoided by keeping the product thin, as the brief proposes: upload, OTP/SSO, and a directory."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence. All three Reddit quotes are complaints that hosting is too expensive. They show price sensitivity and willingness to stay on free tiers, not demand for a new paid entrant. One quote actually supports the incumbents ('it comes with tools that save me time, which is the main reason I pay for it'). The brief also claims 'at least seven well-capitalized direct competitors' but lists only five, and cites a 'race to the bottom' Reddit comment with no source link.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with no clear wedge. Idea A's demand evidence is also thin: one vendor-curated testimonial on Volly's own site and one older Reddit post about sharing tools, with no proof anyone pays a recurring fee. Idea A also carries real security liability, shown by Perch's disclosed sandbox escape. Idea A wins mainly because Idea B's structure (switching friction, free incumbents, low ARPU, heavy infrastructure) is clearly worse for landing a paying customer in 90 days, not because Idea A's evidence is strong."
}
```
